title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists
abstract: arXiv:2608.20918v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Organizations maintain task-specific adapters for open-weight language models, and each new base-model release forces a migration decision: retain existing specialists, port adapters, refresh from preserved behavior, or retrain. Prior transfer work evaluates isolated model pairs, without studying these choices across real model release sequences. We present UpgradeBench, a decision-driven longitudinal benchmark covering four consecutive Qwen releases, one continuation checkpoint, six tasks, and two model sizes, augmented by OLMo checkpoints with known training lineage. The benchmark disentangles three core questions: whether a new checkpoint improves fixed-recipe retrained specialist performance, whether specialization assets transfer across versions, and what recovery resources are usable. tldr: 本文提出UpgradeBench，一个纵向基准测试，系统评估新基础模型发布时如何决策升级或迁移微调LLM专家，揭示升级收益因任务、规模和发布而异，并提供决策指导。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces UpgradeBench, a longitudinal benchmark that systematically evaluates decisions for upgrading or migrating fine-tuned LLM specialists upon new base-model releases, revealing that upgrade gains vary by task, scale, and release, offering decision guidance.
